title: Code Review & Collaboration

Demonstrated all lesson principles: appreciation first, collaborative language, specific suggestions, appropriate humility. Excellent self-awareness and meta-cognition.

key_takeaways: Code review serves dual purposes: quality gate (catching bugs) and learning opportunity (knowledge transfer)
GitHub provides three review actions: Approve (ready to merge), Request Changes (blocking issues), Comment (non-blocking feedback)
Constructive feedback structure: appreciation → observation → impact → suggestion → invitation to discuss
Line comments address specific code issues; review-level comments address overall approach and architecture
Start responses to review feedback with gratitude, even when feedback is difficult to receive
PR update workflow: fix → commit → push to same branch → comment explaining changes → re-request review
Explain reasoning when domain knowledge or tradeoffs aren't obvious; just fix when improvement is clear
Self-review with fresh eyes catches 30-40% of bugs before others see them

catchbook_deliverable.description: Self-reviewed first CatchBook PR with professional-quality line comments. Identified documentation ambiguity in branch naming conventions. Demonstrated code review practices that will be applied to all 140+ future CatchBook modules.

objectives_met: Understand the purpose and benefits of code review for software quality
Leave constructive comments on GitHub PRs (line comments, review comments)
Use GitHub review tools: approve, request changes, comment
Apply code review best practices (kind, specific, actionable feedback)
Respond to review feedback professionally and implement requested changes
Push additional commits to update an open PR
Understand when a PR is ready to merge vs needs more work
